title: 1981 Toyota Land Cruiser FJ45
story: The FJ45 has long held a special place in the collector 4x4 world — produced in far smaller numbers than the FJ40, the long-wheelbase pickup pairs Toyota's legendary durability with genuine work-truck capability. This 1981 example is one of the final years of production, carrying the proven 4.2L 2F inline-six, a four-speed manual, and factory four-wheel-drive.

It's been thoughtfully upgraded rather than left bone stock: an Old Man Emu suspension improves ride quality and articulation without sacrificing reliability, and 33-inch BFGoodrich Mud-Terrain tires add capability while keeping the truck's classic proportions. Power steering and power brakes make it easy to drive day to day.

The seller notes it was restored at some point in its life, though documentation on that work isn't available, and mileage is TMU (true mileage unknown). It carries a clean South Carolina title — an honest, driver-quality FJ45 rather than a six-figure frame-off build.
